title: Stop subagents after repeated identical unrecovered errors
description:
### Context
A worker can repeat the same failed tool action many times without new evidence, amplifying latency and token use.

### Scope
Track privacy-safe error fingerprints and stop one worker after a bounded sequence of identical unrecovered failures. Reset the count when materially different evidence or a successful recovery occurs.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run a worker against a missing path without a retry breaker. Observe repeated identical failed reads continuing until general timeout or resource exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated identical failures trigger a structured stop before general resource exhaustion; successful recovery or changed input resets/changes the fingerprint; raw payloads are not stored; partial output survives; deterministic loop tests pass.

title: Open provider venue circuits on deterministic availability failures
description:
### Context
Routing quality history is model-family based and cannot represent a provider venue whose shared quota or credentials are currently unavailable. Repeatedly switching models on the same venue repeats deterministic failures.

### Scope
Add an expiring health circuit keyed by provider venue. Classify deterministic quota, credit, authentication, and availability failures; reject affected venue candidates with a visible reason while leaving other venues for the same model family eligible.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic provider failure opens a bounded circuit; subsequent routes exclude all affected-venue models and show reason/expiry; success or expiry closes the circuit safely; local and subscription venues remain eligible; routing tests pass.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Implemented in 3283cbe and merged at cdf85b87e053bb0c2d5ef0ddd62798fe3406e4e5. Exact-provider circuits classify bounded quota/credit/authentication/502-504 availability errors; persist only enum/timestamps in locked atomic mode-0600 state; expire by class with one-hour cap; filter all affected-provider route candidates while preserving same-family other venues; close on success; retain providerFailureClass in invoke/subagent metrics. RED/GREEN focused gate: 143 tests, Ruff, config/shell/diff checks passed. Bounded Luna review timed out at 120s without findings; no unchanged retry. Deployed synthetic proof opened credit circuit, visibly blocked 7 olla-cloud targets, preserved OpenAI/local candidates, closed on success, and left empty state without raw error text.
close_reason: Provider-scoped expiring circuits, deterministic classifiers, private concurrent state, routing isolation, success closure, telemetry, docs, tests, deployment, and live synthetic proof integrated.

title: Paginate improvement trace discovery and report lower bounds
description:
### Context
The improvement scanner caps discovery at a fixed trace count and can silently omit sessions before grouping. Per-session limits are surfaced, but global cohort truncation is not.

### Scope
Paginate trace discovery across the requested bounded window or stop at an explicit operator limit while preserving a truthful lower-bound report.

## Steps to Reproduce
Choose a bounded cohort larger than the scanner trace cap and compare API session IDs with scan output. Observe omitted sessions without a global truncation warning.
acceptance_criteria: Scanner traverses all pages for a bounded cohort or reports the exact global limit and continuation state; output distinguishes total available, scanned, attributable, and unattributed traces; per-session caps remain visible; deterministic multi-page tests pass.

title: Finalize Langfuse root traces before short-lived worker exit
description:
### Context
Short-lived execution-shaped traces can have blank names or no finalized root agent observation. Deferred fire-and-forget shutdown is a plausible loss seam.

### Scope
Make root finalization and Langfuse shutdown deterministic for headless and delegated worker processes without delaying normal interactive shutdown unnecessarily.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run several short-lived headless workers and inspect finalized traces. Observe blank trace names or missing root agent observations before deterministic shutdown is added.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated short-lived worker tests produce one named root observation per execution trace; process exit awaits bounded finalization; timeout/failure is visible without hanging the parent; focused live smoke and regression tests pass.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Final local-seam re-evaluation (2026-08-05) against installed pi-langfuse 1.5.7 and Pi 0.83.0: agent_end awaits root finish but schedules shutdownRuntime(sessionId) through unawaited setTimeout. Pi does emit session_shutdown before ordinary exit and the package awaits global shutdown there, but package root exposes no worker-specific finalization handle, completion status, or timeout result; bounded shutdownRuntime/withTimeout remain private. pi-setup therefore cannot guarantee or prove one finalized named root per short-lived worker, especially abnormal child termination, through supported public APIs. Required owner contract: bounded public finalizeRun/shutdown promise with worker identity, first-class lifecycle completion/failure, and no global interactive latency. Private imports, monkeypatching, arbitrary delay, or copied tracing are not acceptable. Deferred as upstream-owned under decision pi-bdyu; no upstream edit, fork, PR, pin, vendor, installed edit, deployment, or push was made.
close_reason: Verified resolved by released pi-langfuse 1.5.8/1.5.9 behavior. Focused source tests passed: agent_end awaits shutdown, one total shutdown deadline, and stalled score HTTP child exits (3/3). Fresh live smoke ran three short-lived headless sessions; each produced exactly one session-matched trace with one named, ended root observation and no shutdown error. Original upstream-contract deferral is obsolete.

description:

### Scope

title: Propagate canonical session identity into every execution trace
description:
### Context
Many root and short-lived execution traces lack session IDs, preventing exact work-item, projection, and outcome correlation.

### Scope
Use the canonical Pi session ID across root agent traces, interactive projections, subagent projections, and workers. Fall back to PI_SESSION_ID when session-manager context is unavailable; never substitute an unrelated current/default session.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run interactive and delegated executions, then inspect their root and projection session fields. Observe execution traces without the canonical Pi session ID.
design: Minimal normalized join: pi-langfuse prefers public SessionManager.getSessionId() over legacy file basename; Archimedes captures existing ephemeral JSON session header and returns childSessionId. Parent subagent-result projection stores childSessionId as sole foreign key. Retain --no-session; no invocationId, traceId transport, parent env protocol, or Pi-core change. Plan: .pi/plans/2026-08-05-upstream-traceability-patches-design-plan.md
acceptance_criteria: Ephemeral pi-langfuse roots emit exact logical Pi session UUID; persistent/older contexts retain file fallback. Archimedes returns optional childSessionId from JSON session header without persisting children. Parent subagent-result projection stores childSessionId and exact Langfuse session lookup returns child details. Parallel results remain aligned; finalization loses no completed observations; regression tests pass.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Final local-seam re-evaluation (2026-08-05) against installed pi-langfuse 1.5.7 and Pi 0.83.0: package root exports only its default registration factory. Root session resolution uses sessionManager.getSessionFile() basename, then falls back through package-internal AsyncLocalStorage/current/default state; it does not consume documented PI_SESSION_ID. pi-setup can attach canonical IDs to local projection observations but cannot inject identity into package-owned root creation through a supported public contract. Required owner contract: public canonical session resolver/context injection accepting exact session-manager identity, PI_SESSION_ID fallback, explicit unavailable state, and concurrent isolation. Private src imports, ExtensionAPI/session-manager impersonation, monkeypatching, or duplicate tracing are not acceptable. Deferred as upstream-owned under decision pi-bdyu; no upstream edit, fork, PR, pin, vendor, installed edit, deployment, or push was made.

title: Support dependent implementation continuation after dirty epic worktree checkpoint
description:
E2E finding from pi-2m1.27 Edabit workflow. Stage 2 implementation succeeded in `.worktrees/epic/pi-2m1` and left expected uncommitted `e2e-test/` changes. Stage 3 depended on those changes, but runner blocked dispatch because the epic worktree was dirty and created blocker pi-ada. The safety check is correct for unrelated/concurrent work, but the orchestration lifecycle lacks a first-class continuation/checkpoint path for serial dependent implementation stages.

Desired behavior: when a dependency stage succeeds and a dependent implementation stage is ready, tooling should either automatically kick the dependent work back to the runner with an explicit continuation mode, or produce a clear orchestrator action with preserved state and recovery options. Better: the underlying tooling should detect the pattern, record a lesson/issue automatically, and choose a safe default when policy allows.

Possible design:
- Add a dependent-stage policy to metadata.pi/worktreePolicy, e.g. `continuation: same-worktree-after-success` or `checkpointPolicy: dirty-worktree-continuation`.
- Runner distinguishes expected dirty worktree from prior successful dependency vs unsafe dirty worktree from unrelated/untracked changes.
- Runner active/ready status explains: preserved changes, source run, dependent bead, allowed next actions.
- If continuation is safe and approved, dispatch dependent stage in same dirty epic worktree.
- If not safe, create a Beads-backed blocker with options: continue in dirty worktree, checkpoint-integrate, spawn continuation worktree, or defer.
- Automatically capture a lesson/follow-up when the runner encounters this missing lifecycle path.

This avoids manual shell workaround and prevents the orchestrator from inventing ad hoc checkpoint integration.
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic test reproduces: implementation stage A succeeds and leaves expected changes in epic worktree; dependent implementation stage B is ready.
- Runner does not silently treat this as an ordinary dirty-worktree failure.
- Runner either dispatches B under an explicit approved continuation policy or creates a precise Beads-backed handoff with preserved state, options, and recovery path.
- Status/TUI/gateway expose the continuation/blocker state clearly.
- A lesson/follow-up artifact is recorded automatically or through a structured runner event.
- No unsafe concurrent write dispatch into dirty worktrees.
- Existing dirty-worktree safety remains for unrelated or conflicting changes.

title: Show current-turn and cumulative subagent tokens

### Context

### Expected Behavior

Callers can select cold one-shot mode with explicit thinking. Archimedes enforces isolation and one-request behavior without an implicit wall-clock deadline.

### Actual Behavior

Baseline subagent input exposes neither one-shot isolation nor explicit thinking control.

title: Keep tracked Beads JSONL synchronized
description:
## Context

The repository tracks `.beads/issues.jsonl` as the portable fresh-checkout graph, but live Beads uses an ignored embedded Dolt database. The tracked export remained at 460 records while live state reached 654 because `export.auto` used its false default and hooks are intentionally absent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `bd stats --json` and observe 654 live issues.
2. Run `wc -l .beads/issues.jsonl` and observe 460 tracked records.
3. Inspect `bd config show` and observe `export.auto = false`.
4. Mutate a Bead and observe the tracked export remain unchanged.

## Expected Behavior

Each Beads mutation refreshes the tracked portable JSONL without silently staging it.

## Actual Behavior

Live Dolt state advances while the tracked JSONL remains stale.

## Scope

Enable native automatic export at the existing tracked path, keep `export.git-add` disabled, refresh the export, and add deterministic fresh-checkout regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked config enables native `export.auto` while `export.git-add` remains false; an isolated bootstrap test proves one Bead mutation updates `issues.jsonl`; current tracked export contains every live regular issue exactly once; fresh-checkout bootstrap, Pi config, focused tests, and full project gates pass.
notes: Root cause confirmed: native `export.auto` was false by default while hooks were intentionally absent. An isolated 460-record bootstrap probe showed mutations left JSONL unchanged; enabling `export.auto: true` changed the same probe to 461 records while `export.git-add: false` preserved review/staging boundaries. Integrated by 309b5be and merge 65d5191. Merged full gate passed config, shell syntax, Ruff, all 553 pytest tests, routing-smoke, role-context-smoke, context-health, Beads lint, and diff checks.
close_reason: Enabled native automatic tracked JSONL export without implicit staging, refreshed portable state, and added fresh-checkout mutation regression coverage. Integrated and fully verified on main at 65d5191.

title: Langfuse flush sends ingestion body above 4.5 MB limit
description:
## Summary

Langfuse flush/shutdown can send one REST ingestion request larger than the server's 4.5 MB body limit. The server returns HTTP 413, and pi-langfuse reports `Failed to flush/shutdown cleanly`, risking loss of buffered telemetry.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate enough buffered Langfuse events for one ingestion payload to exceed 4.5 MB.
2. Trigger runtime flush or shutdown.
3. Observe `POST /api/public/ingestion` return HTTP 413 with `rawBody: Body exceeded 4.5mb limit`.
4. Observe `_LangfuseAPIError` from `Ingestion.__batch`, propagated through `fallbackToRestIngestion` and `shutdownRuntime`.

## Expected Behavior

Flush partitions or otherwise bounds ingestion requests below the service body limit and completes without dropping buffered events.

## Actual Behavior

Fallback REST ingestion submits an oversized body; shutdown logs a 413 failure and does not flush cleanly.

## Evidence

Observed 2026-08-05 against `https://langfuse.st5ve.com/api/public/ingestion`: HTTP 413 Request Entity Too Large, `Body exceeded 4.5mb limit`. Stack points to `@langfuse/core` ingestion via `pi-langfuse/src/langfuse.ts` `fallbackToRestIngestion` and `shutdownRuntime`.

## Scope

Find shared batching seam and enforce a byte-safe request ceiling there. Preserve event ordering and surface any irreducible single-event oversize failure.
acceptance_criteria:
A regression check reproduces a multi-event ingestion payload exceeding 4.5 MB.
All generated REST ingestion requests stay below a documented safe byte ceiling.
Every event is sent exactly once and in order across resulting requests.
An individually oversized event fails explicitly without blocking diagnosis of remaining buffered events.
Flush/shutdown completes without HTTP 413 for the reproduced case, and focused tests pass.
notes:
2026-08-07 root-cause inspection: shared src/langfuse.ts ingestBatch() sends JSON.stringify({batch}) once for both score ingestion and REST fallback, with no byte partitioning. Current Langfuse POST /api/public/ingestion API reference documents a 3.5 MB total batch limit, stricter than the observed self-hosted 4.5 MB rejection. Planned minimum fix: private stable greedy partitioning at a 3,000,000-byte UTF-8 body ceiling, preserving order/exactly-once for sendable events and returning explicit local errors for individually oversized events while continuing with later sendable events. No config/public API.
Human approval pi-5d14 recorded with UI resolver provenance.
2026-08-07 completed. Root cause was shared src/langfuse.ts ingestBatch() serializing one unbounded JSON request for both scores and self-hosted REST fallback. Current primary POST /api/public/ingestion reference documents a 3.5 MB total batch limit. Fork-local draft https://github.com/stvhay/pi-langfuse/pull/2 is OPEN+DRAFT at ba058b3 against main with one commit, four files, and zero reviewers; no upstream PR exists. Fix greedily splits exact UTF-8 bodies at 3,000,000 bytes, preserves order, returns privacy-safe local 413 errors for irreducible single events while continuing later sendable events, keeps score envelope IDs stable across partial retries, reserves half remaining shutdown budget for delivery, and aborts stalled visibility GETs at that subdeadline. Upstream candidate passed 64 tests, typecheck, package dry-run, and final Terra PASS. Pullable vendor/pi-setup f156802 preserves logical session and score-ID patches and passed 65 tests/typecheck/package dry-run. Pi-setup ea74089 pins/regenerates the exact four-file npm 1.5.9 production projection and classifies exact package state with forced whole-patch reverse/forward dry-runs; clean/current skip reinstall while marked or unmarked partial states reinstall with rollback through install, patch, and evaluator failures. Pi-setup passed 579 tests, Ruff, config/shell, routing/role evals, fuzz=0 exact vendor match, fresh previous-patch migration, idempotent repeat, and final Terra PASS. Live installed-source proof against a synthetic 3.5 MB server guard split an original 4,801,126-byte multibyte fallback into ordered 2,400,666- and 2,400,471-byte requests with all five event IDs exactly once; a 3,000,240-byte single event returned explicit local 413 diagnostics while the later event was delivered. Subscription-backed reviews used request/time liveness bounds with no token/cost caps.
close_reason: Legacy Langfuse REST ingestion is byte-bounded below the documented server limit with ordered delivery, dedupe-safe retries, explicit oversized-event diagnostics, rollback-safe deployment, reviewed fork staging, and installed-source proof.

description:

title: Upgrade Pi after patched transitive security release
description:
### Context
The current documented Pi 0.83.0 baseline publishes an npm shrinkwrap containing undici 8.5.0 and brace-expansion 5.0.7. npm audit reports one moderate and two high vulnerabilities; Pi 0.83.0 is currently the latest release, and its shrinkwrap prevents root overrides from replacing those nested packages. CI uses the package only for tests with lifecycle scripts disabled, but the deployed Pi runtime carries the same versions.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Install @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.83.0.
2. Run npm audit --omit=optional.
3. Observe GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272 and related undici advisories plus GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg/GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 for brace-expansion.

### Scope
Track an owner release that updates the published shrinkwrap, then update the tested/deployed Pi baseline without weakening integrity or suppressing audit evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A released Pi package pins undici >=8.9.0 and brace-expansion >=5.0.9 (or later non-vulnerable versions); tracked runtime pin and docs update together; npm audit no longer reports these advisories; extension and full project gates pass.

title: Isolate provider circuit state in deterministic tests
description:
### Context
Provider-circuit review failures correctly open private runtime state, but unrelated routing unit tests read that live state and fail. Test execution must not depend on operator runtime circuits.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a provider circuit in the default private runtime directory.
2. Run routing tests that expect the affected venue to remain eligible.
3. Observe deterministic assertions fail because production circuit state excludes the venue.

### Scope
Give deterministic tests a private per-test provider-circuit directory while retaining explicit integration coverage of persisted circuit behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Project tests use a per-test private provider-circuit directory unless a test supplies an explicit state path; a live open circuit cannot change routing-unit expectations; provider-circuit integration tests still cover real state behavior; focused and final gates pass.
notes: Implemented at b3b0254: one autouse pytest fixture assigns a private per-test AGNT_PROVIDER_CIRCUIT_DIR; explicit state-path and subprocess integration tests remain unchanged. TDD RED was KeyError with ambient variable absent. GREEN: 139 focused tests passed; a seeded ambient openai-codex circuit could not alter routing expectations; Ruff and diff checks passed.
close_reason: Per-test provider-circuit isolation implemented and verified in b3b0254.

title: Align GPT-5.6 context metadata with full model window
description:
### Context

OpenAI documents GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna with 1,050,000-token context windows. Pi intentionally defaults direct OpenAI models to 272,000 to remain in the short-context pricing tier, and pi-setup mirrored that operational cap. The user approved opting the subscription-backed openai-codex venue into full context so observational-memory can compact near measured attention degradation instead of at 136,000.

### Scope

Add tracked model overrides for openai-codex GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna at 1,050,000, align routing catalog metadata, and change observational-memory ratio from 0.5 to 0.25. Preserve 81,000 fallback and low-thinking Sol workers. Document 262,500 effective threshold and 272,000 long-context pricing boundary. Do not change provider, credentials, worker model, or output limits.
design: Use supported pi models.json modelOverrides rather than redefining providers. Keep runtime and agnt catalog context metadata identical. Ratio mode remains global and computes floor(active contextWindow × 0.25); for GPT-5.6 this is 262,500, below the 272,000 API long-context pricing threshold. Verify with a fresh isolated Pi model listing and fresh deployed observational-memory startup.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked pi/agent/models.json overrides openai-codex gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, and gpt-5.6-luna to contextWindow 1,050,000 without credentials or provider redefinition; pi/agent/catalog.json matches all three; observational-memory ratio is 0.25 and fallback remains 81,000; deterministic tests prove 1,050,000 × 0.25 = 262,500 and config/docs consistency; Pi config, focused tests, deployment, fresh model listing, and fresh observational-memory startup verification pass.
notes: Implemented and deployed in commit 7f19c296e97c21c2c747d9a5b256d066f28dccc3. TDD RED: focused tests failed on missing models.json and ratio 0.5. GREEN: 2 focused tests passed; affected-neighbor matrix passed 50/50. Final candidate gate passed config, shell, Ruff, all 518 pytest tests, routing-smoke, role-context-smoke, strict context-health, and diff checks. Deployment proof: all three openai-codex GPT-5.6 models list 1.1M/128K; fresh Pi session loaded contextWindow=1,050,000, ratio=0.25, threshold=262,500, and unchanged low-thinking Sol worker configuration.
close_reason: Full GPT-5.6 context overrides, aligned routing metadata, 0.25 memory ratio, docs, tests, deployment, and fresh runtime proof completed.

title: Run observational-memory workers on bounded low-thinking Sol
description:
### Context

Without a model override, pi-observational-memory background observer, reflector, and dropper stages use the active session model, though source defaults their thinking to low. Recent sessions ran 25 hidden stages in one hour. Compaction itself renders prepared memory and does not call a model.

### Scope

For the trial, pin observational-memory background workers to openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol at low thinking. The package exposes one shared model setting, so this applies to observer, reflector, and dropper rather than reflection alone. Do not imply that thinking changes compaction.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked configuration pins provider openai-codex, model gpt-5.6-sol, and thinking low; tests reject accidental medium/high thinking and document that the setting applies to observer/reflector/dropper workers rather than compaction; a fresh-session bounded check confirms effective configuration and preserves memory lifecycle behavior; Pi config checks pass.
notes: Implemented in d496edd and merged at 84ce1fbe4c197a79187b5a711cf2bbdce907d090. RED: focused test failed on missing model override. GREEN/post-merge: 21 focused tests plus config/shell/diff checks passed. Deployed tracked config. Fresh no-session Pi process loaded contextWindow=272000, threshold=136000, ratio mode 0.5, and shared worker model openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol thinking low.
close_reason: Low-thinking Sol worker override, scope documentation, deployment, and fresh-process effective-config proof integrated.

title: Scale observational-memory compaction to the active context window
description:
### Context

pi-observational-memory 3.0.3 defaults to a fixed 81,000-token calibrated trigger intended for roughly 128K–200K context models, while tracked gpt-5.6-sol and related models expose 272K windows. The exact installed package matches upstream commit 27a5195.

### Scope

Configure tracked Pi settings to use ratio-mode compaction at 0.5 so the trigger follows each active model context window with conservative headroom. Preserve V3 observation, reflection, pool, passive, and debug defaults unless tests prove another change is required.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked configuration sets compactAfterTokensMode=ratio and compactAfterTokensRatio=0.5; deterministic tests prove the effective threshold is 136,000 for a 272,000-token model and falls back safely when context is unavailable; package provenance and exact README guidance are recorded; Pi config checks pass.
notes:
Implemented in b345470 and merged to main. RED: focused test failed on missing compactAfterTokens. GREEN/post-merge: 18 focused tests passed; config and diff checks passed. Tracked ratio=0.5 yields 136,000 for Sol 272,000 and explicit 81,000 fallback. Exact npm 3.0.3 source provenance documented at commit 27a5195.
2026-08-05 user-provided research note: gpt-5.6-sol attention degradation appears around 250k-300k tokens, described as roughly 25%-30% of its context window. Current tracked catalog advertises 272k and ratio 0.5 resolves to 136k: conservative against the absolute threshold but not against the proportional threshold (68k-82k). Do not retune until actual-versus-advertised context semantics are reconciled.
close_reason: Ratio-mode compaction configuration, fallback, provenance docs, and deterministic checks integrated.

title: Calibrate Codex review routing by latency-adjusted yield
description:
## Context

Subagent projections and local metrics now carry normalized provider, model, target, duration, and thinking-level fields from pi-4tg9.8. Current review routing prefers `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra`; Luna is qualified but not the default. Existing `code-review-smoke` still checks only non-empty output, so routing lacks matched quality-and-latency evidence.

## Scope

Create a paired bounded-review evaluation for Terra and Luna using identical seeded defect and clean-control packets, matched effective thinking and output limits, and fixed time limits. Measure completion latency, timeout rate, confirmed unique findings, false positives, and verification effort. Keep Terra as default unless a predeclared latency-adjusted-yield threshold passes, then change only the bounded review cohort supported by evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Eval contains representative seeded defects and clean controls; Terra and Luna run matched packets at matched effective thinking and output limits; recorded dimensions are validated rather than assumed; results report wall latency, timeout rate, confirmed unique findings, false positives, and verification time; repeated runs separate model effect from provider noise; routing changes only when a documented quality floor and latency-adjusted-yield threshold pass; high-risk escalation behavior remains intact.
notes: Updated 2026-08-06 after pi-4tg9.8 and the Terra-first review portfolio landed. Original Sol-default and missing-dimensions wording is superseded; the evaluation gap remains.

title: Reduce progress-only model turns and batch independent tools
description:
### Context

Recent telemetry contained 79 todo-only model turns plus many read-only and bash-only turns. Progress visibility remains required, but model-visible progress calls and serial independent reads/checks add avoidable round trips.

### Scope

Derive progress from execution events where supported; otherwise update todos at meaningful phase boundaries rather than micro-steps. Batch independent reads, searches, and checks in one turn while preserving ordering, safety, and immediate completion visibility. Put concise always-applicable rules at the lowest-cost instruction seam and keep detailed methods in token-saver rather than loading the full skill by default.
acceptance_criteria: Representative multi-step workflows expose current phase and completion without progress-only turns between every tool; independent read-only calls are batched; ordered mutations, approvals, and safety gates remain serialized; token-saver covers detailed batching/progress guidance; default instruction growth is bounded and context-health passes; a deterministic or telemetry-backed eval measures fewer single-tool todo/progress turns without reduced task visibility.
notes:
Human-approved from the bounded 2026-08-05 latency review; private trace payloads remain outside Beads.
Implemented in 634629e and merged at 77bb8785f54302cc4d2a315249f85b60199d8cb2. Added two bounded always-on rules (230-byte AGENTS.md growth), detailed token-saver guidance without frontmatter growth, and payload-free RPC activity derived from concurrent tool lifecycle events while preserving todo/subagent widgets. RED then GREEN: 27 focused tests; config/shell/diff/context checks passed. Deployed. Fresh bounded Sol-low workflow used one assistant tool turn for three independent reads, two assistant messages total, and zero todo-only turns; this is representative proof, not a population estimate against the historical 79-turn baseline.
close_reason: Phase-boundary guidance, batched reads, execution-derived RPC progress, tests, deployment, and representative fresh-workflow proof integrated.

title: Separate repair checks from final release verification
description:
### Context

Recent telemetry showed repeated broad verification against an already-red baseline. Three failed full-suite runs consumed 284 seconds, and one unchanged TypeScript baseline failure was rediscovered four times. Repair loops need focused evidence without weakening final completion gates.

### Scope

Establish the relevant baseline once per isolated work item or worktree. During repair, rerun only checks affected by the change or failed finding. Run the complete required release gate once for the final candidate, and rerun it only when that candidate changes. Classify unchanged baseline failures separately from task regressions and preserve their evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Workflow guidance and evals distinguish baseline, focused repair, and final release verification; unchanged baseline failures are reported separately and do not trigger identical broad reruns; each repair still leaves focused executable evidence; the final candidate receives every required full gate; a representative pre-existing-failure scenario passes without weakening completion claims.
notes:
Human-approved from the bounded 2026-08-05 latency review; private trace payloads remain outside Beads.
Implemented in fe788d2 and merged at 6979d8ed5906dc015a0ad820baa997b4ebdb00db. Four workflow skills now share baseline-once, focused-repair, unchanged-baseline classification, and one full gate per stable final candidate. Task-regression PASS is separated from release NOT_VERIFIED; required red gates never become PASS. RED then GREEN: 21 focused deterministic tests; Luna verification-phases-smoke passed twice on final skill candidate; config/context/diff checks passed. Deployed tracked skills.
close_reason: Verification phases, truthful pre-existing-failure classification, focused repair evidence, final-gate contract, tests, eval, and deployment integrated.

title: Preserve private runtime store during Pi config deployment
description:
### Context

`scripts/update-pi-config.sh` deploys tracked Pi configuration with `rsync --delete` while promising to preserve runtime state. The top-level `runtime/` store is not excluded.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create `<PI_CONFIG_DEST>/runtime/<repo-hash>/metrics/...`.
2. Run `scripts/update-pi-config.sh`.
3. Observe repeated `cannot delete non-empty directory: runtime/...` warnings; non-excluded runtime kinds are eligible for deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level runtime/ is excluded from deployment deletion; a regression test proves a sentinel survives and deployment emits no runtime deletion warning; shell/config checks pass.
notes: Root cause: rsync --delete excluded nested metrics/ but not top-level runtime/, so runtime kinds such as runs were deleted while metrics directories emitted non-empty warnings. Commit d03f552 adds runtime/ exclusion and a real temp-destination sentinel regression. RED: focused test failed with FileNotFoundError after sentinel deletion. GREEN: 11 update-script tests, all 484 pytest tests, Ruff, shell syntax, config validation, dry-run exclusion proof, and diff checks passed.
close_reason: Runtime store is deletion-protected with regression coverage; commit d03f552.

title: Add requirement simplification review skill
description:
### Context
A successful architecture review simplified an implemented runtime by tracing complexity back to explicit and implicit requirements, challenging one assumption at a time, maintaining a quantitative deletion/future-avoidance scoreboard, and closing with aligned design docs and implementation Beads. Existing architecture skills focus on deepening modules, not requirement archaeology and durable simplification decisions.

### Scope
Add a repository-owned Pi skill and baseline scenario that generalize this method. Keep it distinct from direct code simplification, generic architecture deepening, and greenfield design. Include conversational one-decision-at-a-time gates, evidence-first codebase inspection, quantitative range accounting, durable decision artifacts, contradiction audit, and follow-up Bead coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A tracked skill has precise positive and negative triggers; a RED scenario records expected weak behavior; workflow requires repository evidence before questioning, one decision at a time with recommendation, separate current-removal and future-avoidance ledgers, and closeout audit/tracking; focused context and skill checks pass; diff is handoff-ready.
notes: Implemented repository-owned explicit skill at pi/agent/skills/requirement-simplification-review/SKILL.md with three RED/behavior scenarios covering first-decision archaeology, deterministic closeout arithmetic/Beads ownership, and near-neighbor refactoring non-trigger. Isolated Pi runs verified existing-review detection and closeout ranges; usage fields were unavailable in emitted message_end events. Independent re-review PASS. Full project verification: 483 pytest PASS, ruff PASS, config/shell PASS, routing-smoke PASS, role-context-smoke PASS, context-health strict PASS with existing discovery-budget warning (5 chars remaining).
close_reason: Added reviewed and evaluated requirement-simplification-review skill in signed commit 1018104; full repository verification and isolated behavior checks pass.

title: Always offer a typed custom response for question prompts
description:
### Context
Human question aborts commonly occur because listed options do not match the intended answer and no usable typed alternative is available.

### Scope
Always render a clear custom-response choice for question prompts. In multi-select mode, allow the typed response to be combined with predefined selections; persist and return the custom text with selected values. Approval actions retain explicit informed-consent semantics and must not interpret arbitrary text as approval.
acceptance_criteria: Single-select questions accept one typed alternative; multi-select questions accept predefined choices plus typed text; empty custom values are rejected clearly; transient and durable results preserve selected and custom values; keyboard/accessibility and regression tests pass.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Integrated source commit fbdca13 and merge b5522b5. RPC and durable questions now always expose typed Other input, preserve selectedOptions/customInput (including explicit empty multi-selection), reject blanks, disambiguate sentinel collisions, and keep approvals confirm-only. Review found four concrete defects; all were fixed and fresh verifier returned PASS. Final candidate gate passed Ruff, all 537 pytest tests, Pi config, shell syntax, routing-smoke, role-context-smoke, action validation, strict context-health, and diff checks. Deployed tracked Pi config locally with live config validation and byte-equality proof. No upstream, installed-package, fork, PR, push, release, vendoring, or remote deployment changes.
close_reason: Integrated b5522b5; reviewed, final gate passed, and tracked Pi config deployed locally.

title: Require explicit single-select or multi-select question mode
description:
### Context
Human question aborts commonly occur because the model presents forced single-choice UI when the user needs multiple selections. This is a cardinality contract defect, not evidence that durable questions are inherently overused.

### Scope
Require the model to declare question selection mode explicitly as single-select or multi-select. Carry that mode through transient and durable question tooling and UI rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Question tool schema requires an explicit selection mode; omission fails with an actionable validation error; multi-select returns all selected values; single-select returns exactly one; durable question records preserve mode; compatibility migration and tests pass.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Integrated on main via b38bfc9. Explicit mode, durable cancellation, TUI/headless upstream delegation, RPC portable flow, and approval semantics verified. Fresh integrated verification: 458 full tests and project checks passed; independent review PASS.
close_reason: Integrated to main with TDD, independent review, and fresh full verification.

title: Classify telemetry errors by outcome and source
description:
### Context
Raw nonzero tool and process observations currently conflate expected negative tests, recovered retries, command mistakes, provider failures, infrastructure faults, agent failures, and unknown states.

### Scope
Add a payload-free taxonomy with expected, recovered, provider, infrastructure, agent, outcome-blocking, and unknown classifications. Preserve raw counts as health signals rather than mistake labels.
acceptance_criteria: Classification rules are deterministic and precedence is documented; expected and recovered failures do not inflate actionable failure counts; provider and outcome-blocking failures remain visible; unknown is retained rather than guessed; synthetic regression cases pass.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Implemented at 4e2fa31: private schema-2 scan features now include additive schema-1 payload-free errorTaxonomy with separate raw/unclassified-raw health counts, deterministic class/source precedence, actionable/non-actionable/unknown totals, and independent outcome-blocking counts. Expected/recovered remain non-actionable; provider/infrastructure/agent remain visible; malformed metadata stays unclassified. Focused TDD and post-integration proof passed 223 tests plus Ruff/config/diff checks. Sol/Luna review workers were unavailable at provider usage cap; fallback local review produced four refuted claims, while root inspection found and fixed empty artifactFailureClass handling. No live deployment or remote change was performed.
close_reason: Payload-free deterministic error taxonomy implemented and verified in 4e2fa31.

title: Evaluate artifact-backed subagent outputs against their contract
description:
### Context
Successful tasks that intentionally return completion status can be scored poor because the evaluator cannot see the parent-owned artifact or requested output contract.

### Scope
Make quality evaluation aware of artifact references and whether the delegated contract requested inline findings, an artifact, status only, or PASS/no-findings.

## Steps to Reproduce
Delegate a task whose contract requests an artifact and status-only return. Persist valid findings but return completion status; observe a poor quality score based only on final text.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator receives bounded artifact content or an explicit unavailable state plus the output contract; status-only success is not penalized when requested; missing required findings still score poorly; deterministic fixtures cover inline, artifact, PASS, and missing-output cases.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Implemented at 635c28f through tracked public Archimedes composition: optional single/per-child output contracts propagate to parent artifacts, schema-2 metrics/compaction, and bounded contract-aware subagent-result evaluation context. Persisted artifacts with null content are explicitly unavailable. TDD and 250 focused tests passed; Ruff/config/diff checks passed. Review found one important artifact-content-state gap and one minor schema-fixture gap; both were fixed and freshly verified, while one task-bound hypothesis was refuted. Remote Langfuse apply and live ~/.pi deployment were intentionally not performed under final-wave boundaries.
Reopened from live report: archimedes.ts throws during extension factory load because pi-archimedes 1.8.3 registers subagent lazily in session_start, while the wrapper assumed synchronous factory registration. Source and deployed wrapper hashes match, confirming a code/test contract defect rather than deployment drift.
Live regression fixed in 2b954dc. Root cause: pi-archimedes 1.8.3 registers subagent lazily inside session_start, but the tracked wrapper required it immediately after factory return. The wrapper now decorates the full upstream tool at the intercepted lazy registerTool call; static ask behavior and local outputContract stripping remain unchanged. Regression fixture reproduces factory-before-session ordering and fresh-session registration. RED reproduced the exact throw; GREEN passed 35 focused tests. Final gate passed all 547 pytest tests, Ruff, config, shell, action validation, routing/role evals, strict context health, and diff/status. Direct local Gemma review PASS. Actual installed-package loader showed zero errors before deployment; after deployment source/live hashes match, live loader reports zero errors, and the previously blocked live agnt/Pi path returned OK through a fresh session. Read-only Langfuse drift check was clean before deployment, so evaluator apply had no changes to write. No push or upstream/package edit occurred.
close_reason: Lazy Archimedes subagent registration fixed, fully verified, and deployed in 2b954dc.

title: Persist delegated results as parent-owned artifacts
description:
### Context
Some workers write full findings themselves and return only status, creating shared-write risk and leaving parent/evaluator output incomplete. Workflow policy already prefers read-only peers and parent persistence.

### Scope
Persist each delegated final output in the parent process before returning, then expose bounded artifact references in the tool result and telemetry envelope. Workers remain read-only unless their task explicitly requires implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Single and parallel delegated outputs are persisted once by the parent; tool results include stable bounded references; partial and failed outputs are preserved with status; private path policy is respected; tests cover concurrent calls and write failure.
notes: Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
close_reason: Implemented, reviewed, verified, merged, and deployed at c7fe568.

comments.author: Steve Hay
comments.text: Implemented at source commit 71da37e and merge c7fe568. Parent tool_result now persists every single/parallel child before metrics, projection, and return under agnt runtime-path delegated-results. Schema-1 mode-0600 JSON retains final/partial/error output and objective status under mode-0700 UUID dirs; atomic hard-link publication is no-overwrite, cleans temp files, and rejects symlink targets. Tool content/details, schema-2 metrics, compact metrics, and subagent-result metadata share bounded runtime:delegated-results refs plus payload-free persistence status. title: Resolve a safe private directory for runtime artifacts
description:

title: Separate objective execution outcome from apparent outcome evaluation
description:
### Context
A subjective evaluator can mark a provider error successful when task context contains prior evidence. Exit status, provider failure state, and explicit human outcome are not consistently visible or authoritative.

### Scope
Record deterministic execution outcome separately from output-quality or apparent-task judges. Explicit closeout outcome remains authoritative; deterministic provider/process failure cannot be overwritten by a positive apparent score.

## Steps to Reproduce
Produce a deterministic provider/process failure whose task context contains earlier success evidence. Observe that the apparent-outcome judge can score success without execution status.
acceptance_criteria: Nonzero exits and explicit provider failures record execution failure before model judging; explicit human outcomes override sampled apparent outcomes; useful partial output may retain a separate quality score; synthetic success, failure, partial, and unavailable cases pass.
notes: Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.

comments.author: Steve Hay

Private scan features now keep executionOutcome, apparentOutcome, finalOutcome, and finalOutcomeSource separate: explicit human closeout stays authoritative, otherwise failed/unavailable execution constrains sampled apparent judgments. Partial output is preserved with visible failure context. Legacy missing execution stays unknown; latest root result wins; subagent quality remains separate. Focused proof: 263 tests passed, Ruff/config/diff checks passed. Two peer reviews found 3 Important cases; all fixed and fresh bounded verifier returned PASS. Deployed tracked Pi config; deployed-byte equality and fresh simulations proved failed/unavailable projection plus apparent-success-to-final-failure precedence.

title: Emit normalized model dimensions on subagent projections
description:
### Context

### Scope

## Steps to Reproduce

title: Bound Langfuse strings without corrupting media extraction
description:
### Context
The current media corruption workaround disables the global string limit, allowing unrelated prompt, output, and system strings to grow without a finite bound.

### Scope
Preserve complete media extraction or media markers while restoring finite limits for ordinary strings and bounded serialization overall.

## Steps to Reproduce
Set a finite global string limit and send a media-bearing prompt to reproduce malformed media extraction; set the limit to off and observe that unrelated strings become unbounded.
acceptance_criteria: On a clean selected pi-langfuse baseline, capture-enabled generation inputs preserve complete valid Base64 Data URI segments through finite ordinary-string shaping so the normal OTel path emits Langfuse media references and persists no raw Base64; surrounding text remains capped at the finite default and redacted; malformed/truncation-damaged candidates become bounded markers; capture-disabled, metadata, model-parameter, error, and other uncaptured paths never preserve media; REST fallback retains/sends no raw Base64 and does not claim retrievability without upload proof; explicit PI_LANGFUSE_MAX_STRING_LENGTH=off remains supported; package and pi-setup focused/full tests pass. S3-compatible storage, retention, and Langfuse v4 are outside scope.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
Human evaluation selected detailed media preservation with finite ordinary strings. Restack .7 alone onto clean upstream v1.5.9; do not consume combined .6/.7 branch. After a package artifact/release, remove pi-setup default off while preserving explicit operator override. Live retrievability smoke waits for user-owned S3 media configuration.
Current @langfuse/otel extractor regex accepts only unparameterized data:<type>;base64,... forms. Generic parameterized Data URIs (for example charset) cannot satisfy upload/reference target on this baseline and must be recognized as candidates but replaced with bounded malformed/omitted marker, never preserved raw. Preserved media content types must use safe MIME token syntax and must not contain secret/path patterns.

title: Pin Pi runtime dependencies for deterministic CI
description:

4. Install @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.83.0 and rerun the affected test files; all 43 cases pass.

### Scope
Track the exact Pi test runtime and Node engine, install them deterministically before pytest in CI, and prevent local ancestor node_modules from masking dependency drift.

Added locked @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.83.0 test runtime, Node 22 dev shell, immutable setup-node v7.0.0 SHA, npm ci --ignore-scripts before pytest, node_modules exclusion, complete remote tarball integrity fields, and clean-HOME test isolation. Focused and full project checks pass.

title: Resolve pi-archimedes Ctrl+V shortcut conflict with built-in image paste

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a normal Pi session with tracked settings that load npm:pi-archimedes.

title: Fix runner tick timeout/misleading not-running response for slow or blocked dispatch
description: Critical bootstrap usability bug observed live: running `pi/agent/bin/agnt work runner tick --json --limit 1` returned `connected=false`, `detail=timed out`, `running=false`, `status=not-running`, while the Pi gateway still reported the runner as `running active=0`. Root cause likely: the client has a 2s timeout and `/v1/tick` executes scheduler work synchronously, so a slow dispatch/blocker path is reported as if the daemon is not running. This gives the operator the wrong next action and forces manual shell debugging.
acceptance_criteria: TDD evidence recorded. A regression test simulates a slow `/v1/tick` or slow dispatch path and verifies the CLI/gateway does not report `not-running` merely because tick exceeded the short request timeout. The tick path should either return quickly with an accepted/background job id, use a longer/operation-specific timeout, expose active/in-progress status, or return an accurate timeout status with a safe next action. Existing status checks must still correctly report genuinely missing/stale services. Relevant runner client/service/scheduler tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed by pi-2m1.19: runner client timeout payload no longer misreports a live slow service as not-running; scheduler/action dispatch fixes also prevent malformed ready items from shadowing valid work.

title: Make runner daemon autonomously dispatch approved ready work without manual tick command
description: Critical bootstrap reliability bug: a healthy project-local runner service can sit at `running active=0` indefinitely because `agnt work daemon serve` starts the HTTP service and joins its thread, but does not run a scheduler loop. Work only advances when an operator manually runs `agnt work runner tick --json`. This violates the harness goal: once approved work is ready and the runner is healthy, it should pick up bounded work automatically without requiring repeated shell commands.
acceptance_criteria: TDD evidence recorded. A regression test proves daemon/service mode schedules bounded ticks on its configured interval while running and accepting work. A healthy runner with approved ready work transitions from running idle to an active run or a durable blocked/error state without a manual `runner tick` command. The scheduler respects paused/draining state, concurrency/active run limits, dry-run semantics if applicable, idempotency, and does not dispatch while leases are draining or service is stopping. Relevant runner scheduler/service/client tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed by pi-2m1.19: daemon serve now starts an autonomous scheduler loop and reports schedulerEnabled; stale worktree blocker pi-76g superseded.

title: Make harness self-recover from drained runner state without manual shell reset
description: High-priority bootstrap reliability bug from live use: after normal Pi restart, the project-local runner can be running but stuck in `draining` with `acceptingNewWork=false`, requiring manual shell commands to stop, archive `.pi/runner`, restart, or POST `/v1/resume`. This makes the harness unable to do work. Root causes observed: the orchestrator extension attaches a new `pi-tui` lease to a runner service that is already drained/draining; startup `ensureDaemon` treats a connected service as good without checking `draining`/`acceptingNewWork`; `/v1/resume`/`runner_resume` appears not to clear `draining`, so a resume request does not restore accepting-new-work state. Fix the runner/orchestrator behavior so a normal Pi restart recovers automatically into a healthy idle service, with no manual shell reset.
acceptance_criteria: TDD evidence recorded. A regression test reproduces a running runner state with `draining=true`, `acceptingNewWork=false`, and/or a stale/new `pi-tui` lease on startup. After the fix, normal orchestrator startup either resumes/undrains the service or safely restarts it so status becomes running, non-draining, acceptingNewWork=true, active=0 without manual shell commands. `/v1/resume` clears `draining` and drain metadata or an explicit undrain endpoint exists and is used. Shutdown remains idempotent and still drains/stops when appropriate. Relevant orchestrator, runner service, runner protocol/client, gateway visibility tests pass. No runtime state reset is required for normal restart recovery.
close_reason: Fixed by pi-2m1.19: runner resume/startup now clears drained state and orchestrator startup resumes or upgrades unhealthy runner services without manual shell reset.

description: Approved execution bead for the harness repair requested by the user. Supersedes/implements follow-up pi-2m1.13 if the runner requires approved metadata at creation time. Fix orchestrator-service startup/shutdown orphaned lease race using TDD: add behavioral regression coverage for shutdown while lease attachment is in flight or just accepted, then change lease tracking/cleanup so pending/accepted leases are released idempotently and polling cannot start after shutdown. Context: Agents can become unpredictable when the runtime environment diverges from assumptions.

Problem: Broken dependencies, provider env vars, wrong Node version, missing Beads/Docker/Pi binaries, or model/provider failures are discovered late during agent work.

Suggested Improvement: Add agnt doctor as a deterministic operational preflight with JSON output, strict mode, actionable remediation, and Node LTS/nvm/home-management checks. Integrate it into agnt invoke/work paths as a preflight/warning surface.

Acceptance Criteria:
- agnt doctor reports checks with status, severity, evidence, and suggested actions.
- Checks include core binaries, git root, Python, Pi, Beads, Node LTS/nvm manager detection, provider env vars, configured model targets, and project verification command presence where practical.
- Node remediation respects home management conventions and never edits shell/home files without explicit repair command and confirmation-oriented output.
- Tests cover report schema, node-version scenarios, env-var redaction, and nonzero strict behavior.
- Docs explain when agents should run doctor after repeated tool/env failures.
close_reason: Added agnt doctor operational preflight with Node LTS/provider/config checks, strict JSON reporting, and invoke/work preflight hooks.

title: Spike FastAPI lesson aggregation server
description:
Context: User wants an immediately deployable Docker Compose FastAPI service to aggregate lessons learned from Pi agents.

Problem: Lessons currently have no central intake server; agents need a simple JSONL-compatible API with provenance.

Suggested Improvement: Add a small deployable FastAPI + Postgres lesson server with /lesson and /lessons endpoints, Docker Compose on an external Caddy network, and local tests/fixture support.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Docker Compose defines FastAPI API, Postgres dependency, external Caddy network, and internal DB network.
- API supports POST /lesson for JSON or JSONL upsert by uuid, GET /lesson by uuid, PATCH /lesson by uuid, and GET /lessons as JSONL.
- Lesson schema includes uuid, date, hostname, project/project_dir, summary/status/tags/payload fields.
- Local tests can run without Docker Compose or with an isolated fixture.
- README documents deployment and Caddy proxy assumptions.

title: Align project-init eval with opt-in GitHub templates
description:
## Context

The `project_init_clean_scaffold` workflow eval required `.github/pull_request_template.md`, while the project-init skill explicitly classifies GitHub templates as opt-in. A compliant fresh init therefore failed the eval by correctly omitting an unrequested file.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `./scripts/eval-workflow-compliance.sh --case project_init_clean_scaffold` against the previous eval contract.
2. Observe project-init create required Pi scaffolding without `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
3. Observe the eval fail with `missing expected scaffold: .github/pull_request_template.md`.

## Expected Behavior

The eval requires standard Pi scaffolding and rejects unrequested opt-in GitHub templates.

## Actual Behavior

The previous eval incorrectly required an opt-in pull-request template.

## Scope

Align the eval with the existing project-init contract; do not broaden standard scaffolding.
acceptance_criteria: `project_init_clean_scaffold` requires all standard Pi scaffolding, does not require `.github/pull_request_template.md`, and rejects that template when the prompt says not to create opt-in GitHub files. A deterministic contract regression test, shell syntax check, focused workflow case, and project verification pass.

title: Keep main orchestration clean with isolated execution worktrees
description:
## Context

The retained `executing_plans_stops_on_main` failure switched the shared checkout from `main` to `create-marker` and created untracked `MARKER.txt`. A branch switch did not isolate filesystem state: the orchestration checkout became dirty and left `main`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the executing-plans workflow from the shared `main` checkout without same-branch implementation authority.
2. Let the agent create and switch to a feature branch in that checkout.
3. Observe the checkout leave `main` and untracked implementation files appear in the shared worktree.

## Expected Behavior

The orchestration checkout stays on clean `main`. Implementation runs in a separate isolated worktree and branch. After an authorized merge, the merged worktree is pruned under the applicable cleanup authority.

## Actual Behavior

The agent switched the shared checkout to a feature branch and wrote implementation files there.

## Scope

Align executing-plans guidance and its workflow eval with the isolated-worktree default. Preserve explicit approval gates for same-branch work, merge, cleanup, and destructive Git operations.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh workflow eval starting from clean `main` leaves the orchestration checkout on `main`, clean, and without `MARKER.txt`; implementation either stops safely or occurs only in a separate worktree/branch. Deterministic context checks and the focused real-model workflow case pass. Worktree pruning occurs only after merge and with applicable cleanup authority.
notes: Human decision 2026-08-06: default implementation uses an isolated worktree; the main orchestration worktree remains clean on `main`; merged worktrees are pruned during authorized cleanup. Same-checkout branch switching is not isolation because untracked files are shared across branch checkouts.

title: Approve revising and implementing pi-4tg9.3 as projection-only worker telemetry: keep parent-correlated projections/metrics/artifacts, suppress redundant ephemeral worker pi-langfuse roots, and record explicit identity fallback/unavailable state?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve revising and implementing pi-4tg9.3 as projection-only worker telemetry: keep parent-correlated projections/metrics/artifacts, suppress redundant ephemeral worker pi-langfuse roots, and record explicit identity fallback/unavailable state?

Context:
Primary Langfuse documentation distinguishes sessions (application-supplied grouping of separate traces) from distributed tracing (explicit trace/parent-span propagation across processes). pi-langfuse is a community integration scoped to one Pi process and documents one trace per prompt grouped by that local Pi session; it cannot infer Archimedes parentage. Current pi-setup emits both uncorrelated child pi-agent roots and parent-correlated subagent-result projections plus local invocation metrics/artifacts. Independent research concludes this duplication, not merely missing IDs, is the architectural error. Projection-only worker telemetry preserves model/provider, usage, cost, elapsed time, outcome, output contract, artifact status, and quality evaluation needed for retrospective performance analysis. It intentionally drops child-internal Langfuse generation/tool waterfall and TTFT until supported distributed trace-context propagation exists.

Options:
- Approve projection-only local implementation
- Reject and stop for another telemetry model

Requested default: Approve projection-only local implementation
Target bead: pi-4tg9.3

Approval preview:
- Action: Amend pi-4tg9.3 acceptance to require attribution for every retained telemetry record; suppress pi-langfuse package registration in known ephemeral Archimedes/agnt workers; add PI_SESSION_ID fallback and explicit unavailable metadata for parent-owned projections; update focused tests/docs; stage and create one local atomic commit after verification.
- Scope: Expected tracked files: pi/agent/extensions/langfuse-config-env.ts, pi/agent/extensions/subagent-error-workaround.ts, pi/agent/bin/agnt_lib/invoke.py, focused tests, pi/README.md and/or docs/SELF-IMPROVEMENT.md, plus Bead notes/acceptance. No installed-package edit, upstream patch/fork/PR, package upgrade, deployment, push, or remote Langfuse mutation.
- Consequences: Removes duplicate unattributed worker roots and makes parent projections/local metrics canonical for retrospective performance analysis. Retains total delegated usage, cost, duration, outcome, model, artifact, and quality data. Child-internal Langfuse generation/tool waterfall and TTFT will no longer be collected for ephemeral workers; supported distributed tracing can restore that later if needed. May make pi-4tg9.4 unnecessary for suppressed worker roots, subject to its separate evaluation.
- Reversibility: Revert one local commit to restore worker package tracing. Future public trace-context propagation can replace projection-only mode without changing historical parent metrics/artifacts.
- Closeout path: Resolve approval; amend Bead; run direct-start; add RED tests; implement minimum guards/resolver metadata; run focused and full verification plus independent review; commit; record outcome; close pi-4tg9.3; then summarize pi-4tg9.4.

title: Approve revised pi-4tg9.3 recommendation: retain deferral, make no misleading partial code change, record that persisted Archimedes worker sessions are a valid separate design improvement, and proceed to pi-4tg9.4?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve revised pi-4tg9.3 recommendation: retain deferral, make no misleading partial code change, record that persisted Archimedes worker sessions are a valid separate design improvement, and proceed to pi-4tg9.4?

Context:
Human correctly challenged the original no-session rationale. Fresh source and independent peer review show removing Archimedes --no-session would give each worker a persisted file and therefore a filename-derived pi-langfuse sessionId. It still does not provide canonical SessionManager.getSessionId identity, PI_SESSION_ID fallback, explicit unavailable reason, invocation/work-item propagation into the worker root, or exact parent projection/root correlation. Archimedes ignores the child JSON session header and SubagentResult exposes no worker session identity. Thus persistence is worthwhile as a separate package design change but is only partial mitigation for pi-4tg9.3 and risks producing separately grouped or double-counted telemetry.

Options:
- Approve revised deferral and proceed to pi-4tg9.4
- Reject and stop to scope upstream package changes

Requested default: Approve revised deferral and proceed to pi-4tg9.4
Target bead: pi-4tg9.3

Approval preview:
- Action: Retain pi-4tg9.3 as deferred, append revised evidence distinguishing worker persistence from complete identity correlation, make no source/package/deployment change, then evaluate pi-4tg9.4
- Scope: Bead evidence/decision only. Does not edit project or installed files, change pi-langfuse/pi-archimedes, create an upstream patch/fork/PR, upgrade packages, deploy, or push.
- Consequences: Avoids claiming closure from a partial worker-ID mitigation. Canonical root/projection/outcome correlation remains blocked pending public resolver and child-correlation contracts. Separate persisted-worker design may be scoped later. pi-4tg9.14 remains blocked.
- Reversibility: Deferral can be reopened when upstream contracts exist or human separately approves bounded upstream package work.
- Closeout path: Resolve approval, append concise generalized evidence to pi-4tg9.3, verify clean workspace, then present pi-4tg9.4 summary before independent evaluation.

title: For pi-langfuse only, how should reviewed fixes pi-4tg9.6/.7 be integrated without submitting an upstream PR?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: For pi-langfuse only, how should reviewed fixes pi-4tg9.6/.7 be integrated without submitting an upstream PR?

Context:
Installed npm pi-langfuse 1.5.7 owns byte calculation, capture-policy shaping, media extraction, and REST/OTel transport inside private handler closures. Local composition can set environment and order the public extension, but cannot correct already-fabricated byte metadata or media corruption without replacing/reimplementing package handlers. Reviewed patch is based on upstream v1.5.9, changes 311 production lines and 75 deletions plus tests/docs, adds no dependencies, and passes 79/79 tests/typecheck/security review. A public stvhay/pi-langfuse fork pinned by immutable SHA is the smallest reproducible immediate path; no PR would be opened. Vendoring copies the package into pi-setup and creates larger update/dependency burden. Waiting preserves current false 26-byte metadata, broad unlimited-string workaround, and discovered metadata/media privacy gaps.

Options:
- Create public stvhay/pi-langfuse fork, no PR; squash/review, pin immutable SHA
- Do not fork or vendor; leave pi-4tg9.6/.7 open until upstream independently releases fixes
- Vendor patched pi-langfuse source inside pi-setup
- Track patch artifact and build patched runtime during deployment

Requested default: Create public stvhay/pi-langfuse fork, no PR; squash/review, pin immutable SHA
Target bead: pi-4tg9.6

Approval preview:
- Action: Choose integration mechanism for reviewed pi-langfuse fixes only; no upstream PR.
- Scope: Fork option creates one public user-owned fork and tracked immutable git pin; vendor option copies package source into pi-setup; patch option adds deployment-time clone/build/apply logic; wait option changes nothing.
- Consequences: Fork means public maintenance ownership and manual upstream security sync, but avoids copied source and is reproducible. Vendor increases repository/code ownership. Patch-at-deploy increases operational/network/build fragility. Waiting leaves two Wave 1 issues and current telemetry/privacy defects open.
- Reversibility: Fork pin can return to npm release; fork deletion requires separate approval. Vendor/patch changes can be reverted. Wait has no mutation.
- Closeout path: Record decision in pi-4tg9.6/.7, then either prepare reviewed immutable source and run live/integrated verification, or mark issues blocked on upstream release.

title: Scope browser evidence checklists to one browser task
description:
### Context
A later browser task can fail initialization because an earlier completed checklist remains active in persistent session state.

### Scope
Add explicit task identity and safe reset or reinitialization semantics without allowing incomplete requirements to be silently discarded.

## Steps to Reproduce
Initialize and audit one browser-evidence checklist, then initialize a different task in the same persistent session. Observe the already-initialized collision.
acceptance_criteria: Completed or audited task state can be replaced explicitly; active unmet requirements require an acknowledged reset; prove/audit operations reject wrong task IDs; persistent-browser regression tests cover sequential tasks.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.

C2 contract dossier (2026-08-04): BetterWright 1.6.3 is the current npm release and public main/tag source. betterwright/pi-extension publicly exports createPiExtension plus tool schemas. Evidence state is private to one factory closure and shared by browser execution, browser_evidence, agent_end completion nudges, and session_shutdown cleanup; no taskId/reset option or API exists. Pi package filtering was verified to disable the package extension entrypoint. A synthetic public-factory harness verified initial proxy forwarding, then disproved safe reset by capture-only reinvocation: fresh task state was invisible to the original browser tool, invisible to the original agent_end gate, and its browser owner was not closed by the original shutdown handler. Therefore an evidence-only wrapper cannot preserve the package contract/lifecycle and is rejected. Required resumption artifact: released BetterWright support for taskId plus acknowledged reset in the original shared closure (or another public reset API preserving all coupled tools/events). description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve narrowly allowlisting ollama.st5ve.com for Langfuse LLM connections and restarting Langfuse services?

Context:
Langfuse rejected the otherwise valid Ollama connection because ollama.st5ve.com resolves to a private/internal IP. Self-hosted Langfuse supports exact-host exceptions through LANGFUSE_LLM_CONNECTION_WHITELISTED_HOST. Set it to ollama.st5ve.com on relevant web/worker services, then restart them. No connection or evaluator was created by the failed request.

Options:
- Approve exact-host allowlist
- Use paid public provider instead
- Cancel setup

Target bead: pi-mg8u

- Consequences: Langfuse gains intentional network access to the Ollama endpoint. Restart may briefly interrupt Langfuse UI, ingestion, and evaluator workers.
- Reversibility: Remove environment variable and restart services; Langfuse resumes blocking endpoint.
- Closeout path: Bead pi-mg8u records applied deployment location, health checks, and successful connection validation.

title: Approve the proposed design for managing @mariozechner/clipboard?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the proposed design for managing @mariozechner/clipboard?

Context:
Recommended design: add the pinned source `npm:@mariozechner/clipboard@0.3.9` to tracked `pi/agent/settings.json`. Pi will install it into `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules`, which bootstrap already preserves; `@pi-archimedes/image-paste` resolves dependencies from that shared package root before its extension loads. Add a focused settings regression test first (observe RED, then GREEN) and document the managed package in `pi/README.md`. Alternatives rejected: (1) relying on Pi core's nested optional dependency does not reliably satisfy Archimedes and can disappear on Pi reinstall; (2) maintaining a separate `~/.pi/agent/package.json` plus bootstrap `npm install` duplicates Pi's package manager and the current manual runtime files are deleted by rsync. This does not deploy to live `~/.pi` and does not address the separate built-in Ctrl+V conflict tracked by pi-2m1.38.17.

Options:
- Approve design and edit tracked files
- Request design changes
- Cancel this task

Requested default: Approve design and edit tracked files
Target bead: pi-5tvh

- Scope: Changes limited to `pi/agent/settings.json`, a focused test under `tests/`, and `pi/README.md`. No live deployment, package installation, git commit, or remote action.
- Consequences: On the next approved deployment and Pi startup, Pi will install the pinned native addon under its user package cache, allowing Archimedes image paste to require it. Startup needs npm/network only when the package is missing.
- Reversibility: Fully reversible by removing the settings entry, test, and documentation note; the runtime package cache can be removed separately if desired.
- Closeout path: Record RED/GREEN evidence, run focused and project checks, inspect git diff/status, then close bead pi-5tvh if acceptance criteria pass.

title: What rollback threat boundary should the approval authority enforce?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: What rollback threat boundary should the approval authority enforce?

Context:
Independent Terra review found that restoring a complete pre-redemption snapshot of runner state, keyring, journal, and anchor makes all local MACs mutually valid and permits replay. No project-local file design can prevent a malicious same-user actor who can atomically roll back every authority file and signing key. It also found a separately fixable HIGH path issue: the HTTP bearer token and parent directories are not descriptor-anchored. The new contained-worker boundary removes bash/process access and denies `.pi/runner`, `.beads`, secrets, and outside-root paths, so a model worker cannot perform full-store rollback. We need decide whether the authority threat model is contained model workers (simple/cross-platform) or malicious same-user filesystem control (requires an external trust anchor and platform tradeoffs).

Options:
- Contained-worker threat boundary (recommended): protect against model/worker forgery, replay, path escape, and partial rollback; treat full same-user rollback of every runner authority file/key as out of scope, document it, and fix token/parent descriptor paths
- macOS Keychain monotonic anchor: store the journal generation/digest outside project files in Keychain and fail closed if unavailable; stronger same-user rollback resistance but macOS-specific and operationally more complex
- External per-user state anchor: store generation/digest under a separate mode-0700 user state root denied to workers; cross-platform and prevents project snapshot rollback, but not a malicious same-user attacker who rolls back both roots
- Pause and design a stronger platform-neutral authority service before continuing

Requested default: Contained-worker threat boundary (recommended): protect against model/worker forgery, replay, path escape, and partial rollback; treat full same-user rollback of every runner authority file/key as out of scope, document it, and fix token/parent descriptor paths
Target bead: pi-2m1.38.43

Approval preview:
- Action: Choose the trust boundary for rollback/replay protection before the final authority primitive correction.
- Scope: Decision only. No source, checkpoint, deployment, runtime, Git, secret, or external-state mutation.
- Consequences: The recommended option keeps the architecture simple and cross-platform while explicitly relying on worker containment; Keychain provides stronger rollback resistance at the cost of platform coupling and operational complexity.
- Reversibility: The boundary can later be strengthened before deployment through a new design/migration. No mutation occurs from answering.
- Closeout path: Record the selected boundary, implement descriptor-safe token/parent handling and any selected anchor, add behavioral tests/docs, independently re-review, then proceed to UI/scheduler/program-authority integration.

title: How should trusted human approval authority cross the Pi UI-to-runner boundary now that independent review proved CLI/Beads provenance is forgeable?

Question: How should trusted human approval authority cross the Pi UI-to-runner boundary now that independent review proved CLI/Beads provenance is forgeable?

- Pause implementation and produce a focused protocol design/review before more source changes
