title: Which exact authority boundary should the GPT-5.6 Sol repair broker have?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: Which exact authority boundary should the GPT-5.6 Sol repair broker have?

Context:
You clarified that the broker should have full write authority and should itself evaluate the justification and impact of allowing each command. This means Sol is a delegated discretionary policy authority, not merely an adviser behind exact-file write restrictions. The remaining choice is whether a small set of human/system authority effects stays structurally nondelegable. The spike remains uncommitted and undeployed.

Options:
- Full project write authority, with code-enforced nondelegable boundaries for Beads/human approvals, secrets, deployment, runner lifecycle, destructive/remote Git, and writes outside the project (recommended interpretation)
- Unrestricted command authority: Sol alone may approve any command/effect available to the process, including system authority, secrets, deployment, lifecycle, remote Git, and outside-project writes
- Full project write authority with a different nondelegable boundary that I will specify

Requested default: Full project write authority, with code-enforced nondelegable boundaries for Beads/human approvals, secrets, deployment, runner lifecycle, destructive/remote Git, and writes outside the project (recommended interpretation)
Target bead: pi-2m1.38.16

Approval preview:
- Action: Define the delegated authority boundary for the exceptional repair broker.
- Scope: Affects the uncommitted repair-broker design only. No command execution, deployment, checkpoint, runner restart, or unrelated mutation occurs from this decision.
- Consequences: The recommended option permits arbitrary project-content writes after Sol approval while retaining structural protection around human authority and high-consequence external/system effects. Unrestricted authority would make Sol the sole gate for all process capabilities and materially weakens human-only and secret boundaries.
- Reversibility: The policy can be narrowed before deployment; widening it later requires another explicit decision and verification.
- Closeout path: Record the human choice, rewrite RED tests and docs to that authority model, remove inappropriate exact-file restrictions, preserve audit/hash/timeout controls, run full verification and adversarial review against the chosen boundary, then use the existing separately scoped checkpoint/deployment gates.

title: What mutation authority should the repair broker have, given that arbitrary exact project-file writes can create delayed execution outside the sandbox?
description:
Beads-backed question request.

Question: What mutation authority should the repair broker have, given that arbitrary exact project-file writes can create delayed execution outside the sandbox?

Context:
The bounded direct-exec broker now passes 33 focused tests, 270 full tests, static/smoke checks, and closes prior shell, path, process, audit, secret, and approval-boundary findings. Independent review found a structural remaining issue: a model-approved exact write to an auto-sourced/imported file (demonstrated with .envrc.d/gh.sh) creates persistence and later executes outside the sandbox. Path allowlists and filename regexes cannot reliably classify every project file's future semantics. The current spike is uncommitted and undeployed; runner is idle. A durable authority model is needed rather than another deny-list patch.

Options:
- Typed operation registry (recommended): keep Sol evaluation, but replace arbitrary project writes with reviewed code-defined repair operations and postcondition checks
- Read-only broker: allow bounded diagnostics only; all mutations stay in the normal runner or human-approved workflow
- Human-confirmed writes: Sol may recommend exact writes, but every write-capable request requires interactive human confirmation before execution
- Keep model-only exact writes with best-effort persistence deny-lists (not recommended; known structural bypass risk)

Requested default: Typed operation registry (recommended): keep Sol evaluation, but replace arbitrary project writes with reviewed code-defined repair operations and postcondition checks
Target bead: pi-2m1.38.16

title: Approve the recommended fail-closed repair-tool spike, local checkpoint, deployment, and reload?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the recommended fail-closed repair-tool spike, local checkpoint, deployment, and reload?

Context:
Pi supports explicit `-e` extensions even with `--no-extensions`, strict TypeBox tools, `pi.exec`, abort signals, and JSON event streams. The safest design is a two-process broker: the orchestrator-only `repair` tool records `{justification, commands, cwd, timeout}`, hashes the immutable request, then launches openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol with no discovered extensions and only a dedicated terminating `repair_decision` tool. The model supplies only approval and optional reason; trusted extension code executes the exact hash-bound commands if approved and fills `result_stdout`, `result_stderr`, and numeric `result_code` (126 refusal, 124 timeout). Every request gets mode-0600 audit artifacts. The model is not a security boundary: code rejects protected actions before model invocation and again before execution. The tool is installed but disabled by default, enabled only by an explicit orchestrator repair-broker flag. This does not replace human approval for protected actions.

Options:
- Approve constrained opt-in repair-broker spike, checkpoint, deploy, and reload
- Approve evaluator-only dry-run spike with no command execution
- Revise design toward broader authority or always-on availability

Requested default: Approve constrained opt-in repair-broker spike, checkpoint, deploy, and reload
Target bead: pi-2m1.38.16

Approval preview:
- Action: Implement and initialize an opt-in GPT-5.6 Sol repair broker in tracked Pi config, verify it, create one scoped local checkpoint on epic/pi-2m1-38, deploy it to ~/.pi, and reload Pi
- Scope: Only `.worktrees/epic/pi-2m1-38/pi/agent/extensions/repair/{index.ts,evaluator.ts,evaluator-system.md}`, `pi/agent/extensions/orchestrator-service.ts`, focused tests, and one repair-tool document; exact final paths may be reduced but not expanded without approval. One local checkpoint commit containing only these verified paths is allowed. Deployment uses that worktree's `scripts/bootstrap-pi-config.sh --apply`, followed by tracked/deployed identity checks and Pi reload. No runner restart/stop/drain, main-checkout source edits, Beads export edits by implementation, push, fetch, merge, reset, clean, rebase, amend, branch/worktree create/delete/move, hooks, launch agents, unrelated cleanup, Edabit changes, or secrets access.
- Consequences: When explicitly enabled, the orchestration session gains one audited exceptional-command surface. It can approve only commands inside a code-defined local project repair envelope. Hard-denied categories include creating/resolving/forging human approvals or editing Beads authority, credential/secret access, network/download/package-install commands, deployment or runner/process lifecycle control, sudo, obfuscation/backgrounding, remote or destructive Git/history/worktree operations, and paths outside the project/audit temp area. The evaluator cannot call bash directly. The spike increases attack surface but remains fail-closed and opt-in; it is not a substitute for human approval.
- Reversibility: The feature is disabled unless explicitly enabled. The local checkpoint remains unpushed and can later be reverted with a separately approved revert commit. Deployment can be replaced by a later verified bootstrap from another tracked checkpoint; audit logs remain as evidence.
- Closeout path: Behavioral RED/GREEN tests cover approved execution, refusal, malformed/empty/conflicting output, protected commands, hash mismatch, timeout/abort, 0600 outputs, audit completeness, and safe-tool/flag gating. Run focused and full project checks, independently review the diff and evaluator prompt, commit only the approved paths, deploy, verify tracked/deployed identity, reload, then run bounded witnesses: harmless approval writes exact stdout/stderr/code and protected-command refusal executes nothing.

description:

Question: You selected a custom budget policy. Which concrete boundary should I implement?

Context:
A hard budget needs an explicit numeric and reset scope. Provider-reported cost is authoritative only after a worker ends, so any per-worker amount is a planning/escalation threshold rather than a mid-stream kill switch; the hard gate applies before the next dispatch. The architecture remediation may involve many bounded workers, so the earlier $25 total may be too restrictive.

- $100 per epic hard cap; warn/escalate before workers projected above $5
- $50 per epic hard cap; warn/escalate before workers projected above $3
- No per-worker threshold; $100 per epic hard cap only
- I will specify a different exact policy and amounts in chat

- Scope: Determines scheduler cost gates and pi-2m1.38's initial budget. Does not dispatch work or spend money.

A per-worker threshold triggers an approval/escalation before unusually expensive planned work but cannot terminate an already-running provider call.
- Reversibility: Amounts can be raised, lowered, or reset through a later recorded human decision; accrued cost evidence is retained.

Question: Which runner execution model should the architecture remediation implement?

Context:

The review requires choosing either a documented serial runner with inert concurrency machinery removed, or genuine asynchronous multi-worker dispatch. The user's stated preference is a simple base architecture with clear state ownership and minimal corner cases.

Options:

- Implement true asynchronous multi-worker dispatch now
- Stage serial simplification first, then require a separate design/approval before async work

title: Approve the focused canonical terminal-artifact finalizer design and direct repair-mode implementation?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve the focused canonical terminal-artifact finalizer design and direct repair-mode implementation?

Context:
Fresh normal-mode witnesses proved immutable provenance is fixed, but also reconfirmed unstable model-prefixed-only terminal artifacts, generic handoff overwrite, and empty closeout/health checks. Three approaches were considered: (A) add canonical copies inline in invoke_run_bundle—smallest but preserves duplicated terminal logic and overwrite defects; (B) recommended: introduce one tested `finalize_invocation_artifacts` path in runs.py that atomically writes canonical response/stderr/metrics, optionally writes compatibility aliases, preserves or appends to worker-authored handoff/lessons, emits structured artifact/transport/semantic checks, and feeds update_run_result once; (C) redesign all six terminal state writers now—architecturally strongest but too broad and high-risk for this slice. The recommended design advances Stage H's single-finalizer architecture without combining event streaming, typed tool policy, retry/requeue, projectRoot/workspaceRoot, or single transition ownership. Successful runs must have passing canonical-artifact/transport/semantic checks; failed/timeout runs preserve precise failed checks and evidence. If metrics are disabled/unavailable, canonical metrics.json records explicit unavailable state rather than disappearing. Existing model-prefixed files remain compatibility copies for old consumers.

Options:
- Approve recommended focused finalizer design and scoped direct implementation
- Request design changes
- Reject

Target bead: pi-2m1.27.87

- Consequences: New run bundles will always expose stable canonical response/stderr/metrics paths, preserve richer handoff/lessons, and record real terminal artifact/transport/semantic checks. Model-prefixed compatibility files may remain. Live behavior does not change until separately approved deployment.

title: Approve checkpoint integration of Stage 2 e2e-test changes so Stage 3 can run?
description:
Beads-backed approval request.

Question: Approve checkpoint integration of Stage 2 e2e-test changes so Stage 3 can run?

Context:
The E2E workflow deliberately made Challenge B depend on Challenge A. Stage 2 completed in the epic worktree `.worktrees/epic/pi-2m1` and left the expected uncommitted `e2e-test/` changes there. When Stage 3 was queued, the runner correctly refused to dispatch into the dirty epic worktree and created blocker `pi-ada` with reason `epic worktree is dirty`. This is a real workflow finding: dependent implementation stages need an explicit checkpoint integration or a designed continuation mechanism. To continue the E2E now, I propose to copy/merge the Stage 2 `e2e-test/` changes from the epic worktree into the main checkout, then clean only those `e2e-test/` changes from the epic worktree so the runner can dispatch Stage 3 cleanly. This does not commit, push, merge branches, delete worktrees, or rewrite history.

Options:
- approve-checkpoint-integration
- defer

Requested default: defer
Target bead: pi-2m1.27.2

Approval preview:
- Action: Checkpoint-integrate Stage 2 e2e-test files from `.worktrees/epic/pi-2m1` into the main checkout, then remove the staged e2e-test working-tree changes from the epic worktree so Stage 3 can run.
- Scope: Only `e2e-test/edabit_challenges.py`, `e2e-test/test_edabit_challenges.py`, and `e2e-test/README.md` in the main checkout and epic worktree. No commit, push, branch merge, worktree deletion, Beads history rewrite, hook install, launch agent install, secrets access, or unrelated cleanup.
- Consequences: The main checkout will gain the Stage 2 e2e-test files as uncommitted changes; the epic worktree returns clean for the runner. This unblocks Stage 3 while preserving evidence of the worktree-policy gap.
- Reversibility: The main checkout additions remain uncommitted and can be removed later with approval; the epic worktree cleanup only removes the copied Stage 2 e2e-test changes after they are saved in main.
- Closeout path: Record the blocker and approval in Beads, verify Stage 2 tests pass in main, verify epic worktree clean, close/supersede `pi-ada`, and let the runner pick up Stage 3.

title: Harden orchestrator-service startup shutdown race in headless RPC
description: Live acceptance for pi-2m1.11 showed the deployed orchestrator-service extension loading in Pi RPC mode, starting the runner, attaching a lease, and draining on shutdown, but the RPC lifecycle emitted session_shutdown before a stable non-draining running observation. The extension continued startup/polling after shutdown and later surfaced `orchestrator-service failed: fetch failed`. Harden session_start/session_shutdown ordering so startup awaits stop if shutdownStarted becomes true, polling is not started after shutdown, and expected already-drained shutdown does not surface a noisy fetch-failed widget.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test simulates shutdown during async startup and verifies no polling starts after shutdown, no fetch-failed widget is shown for expected drain/stop, lease/drain behavior remains idempotent, and normal session_start still starts/attaches/refreshes runner status.
close_reason: Hardened orchestrator-service startup/shutdown ordering so headless RPC shutdown aborts in-flight startup, prevents polling after shutdown, releases any late lease, requests drain idempotently, and suppresses expected already-stopped/fetch-failed shutdown errors.

title: Reuse unchanged skill instructions within a session
description:
### Context
Long sessions repeatedly read identical workflow skill files, adding tool calls and context without new information.

### Scope
Reuse an already loaded skill body within the same session when path and content version are unchanged. Invalidate on file change and preserve explicit reread capability for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Second unchanged load reuses session state without another full read; file modification invalidates the entry; cache never crosses unrelated sessions; behavior is visible enough to debug; focused tests pass.
notes:
Human-approved generalized retrospective finding; private trace evidence remains outside Beads.
C4 contract result (Pi core 0.83.0, upstream v0.83.0 commit 845d6ff1f6643aba440341cce877ce1c43ebbc39): BLOCKED on unsupported local seam. Synthetic faux-provider proof observed two unchanged /skill expansions causing 2 synchronous skill-file reads and 2 full bodies in user context; two model-selected built-in read calls caused 2 file reads, 2 tool results, and 2 full bodies in tool context. Public input/getCommands exposes raw input and skill provenance only: continue preserves canonical behavior but rereads; transform can avoid the read only by duplicating full content or changing canonical semantics. Public read factories can delegate exact behavior, but every call must return content; full cached content saves no context, while a compact marker changes general read semantics. No tracked workaround or commit created. Smallest resumption: released Pi-core first-class, branch/compaction-aware session skill loader shared by model-selected loading and /skill expansion, with canonical formatting/errors, file-version invalidation, reload/session invalidation, explicit force-reread, and built-in general read left unchanged.
Contract investigation proved no supported local cache seam. /skill expansion privately rereads and reinjects full content; model skill loading uses ordinary read tool. Public input/getCommands cannot delegate canonical expansion; read override either saves no context or breaks general read semantics. Required Pi-core change: first-class session-local skill loader with branch/compaction awareness, file-version invalidation, explicit force reread, canonical formatting/errors, and ordinary read unchanged. Synthetic focused upstream tests passed.
Reopened: upstream source commit exists locally but is not yet independently reviewed, consumable by pi-setup, integrated, or verified.
Wave 1 completion boundary clarified by user on 2026-08-04: package-owned work is complete after an isolated local source patch satisfies acceptance, focused/full checks pass, and independent review passes. Wave 1 does not require an upstream PR, fork, push, release, package pin, vendoring, remote publication, or runtime deployment. Any later package consumption is separate follow-up work. Historical plan stop clauses requiring release/consumption are superseded for pi-4tg9.7, pi-4tg9.20, and pi-4tg9.26.
Wave 1 local-source completion: Pi-core branch feat/pi-4tg9-26-skill-session-cache through 35b9eb56. Final reviews found and fixed context-delivery commit timing, pre/post-compaction ordering, queued full-body and reuse-marker delivery, pending cleanup, disabled model invocation, dual tool collisions, descriptor revision races, deleted-skill truthfulness, and multipart duplication. Final changed suites 56/56 and broader focused 109/109 PASS; diff/status clean. Root tsgo currently reports one unchanged packages/ai/test/openai-completions-tool-choice.test.ts TS2345 outside the patch; no changed-area type errors. title: Decide Beads role configuration for pi-setup
description:
Why:
Repeated Beads commands in the production soak emitted: beads.role not configured (GH#2950). The warning adds noise to agent runs and may hide more important diagnostics.

What:
Decide whether this repository should set a repo-local beads.role value such as maintainer or contributor, document the decision, and apply it only if approved.

Acceptance criteria:
The decision is recorded; either the warning no longer appears in normal bd commands or the project documents why it is intentionally left unset.
notes: Decision: set repo-local git config beads.role=maintainer. Rationale: pi-setup is maintained directly in this checkout and the production soak Beads were created/owned by maintainer identities; maintainer matches the repository's maintenance role. Scope: local repository config only (.git/config), not a tracked secret or Beads remote/history change. Verification: git config --show-origin --get beads.role returned file:.git/config maintainer; bd ready no longer emitted the GH#2950 role warning; bd show pi-4lb --json returned valid JSON; agnt work health --json exited 0.
close_reason: Configured repo-local beads.role=maintainer and verified normal bd commands no longer emit the role warning.
